            The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises  on the recommendations contained in
the  200th      Report (of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry) on  Demands for Grants (2007-08) pertaining to the then Ministry of Small
Scale Industries. 
 
2.         Action Taken Notes have been received from the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises   in respect of the   recommendations contained in the Report.  
These have been categorized as follows:
 
Chapter -I- The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry.
 
            The Committee is pleased to observe that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations as mentioned in the Chapter – I of the Report.        
Chapter -II- The recommendation/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the Government's replies.
 
            In respect of these recommendations the Committee is convinced with the logic and explanations advanced  by the Ministry and therefore does not want to pursue
them for the present.
Chapter -III- The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee has either not accepted replies of the Ministry or has asked the Ministry to review its
reply.
            The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of recommendations contained in Chapter – III and desires that the Ministry should furnish logical
explanations  therefor.
Chapter -IV- The recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Ministry have not been received.
 
                In respect  of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV, the Ministry has  either   furnished the interim replies or couched its language in  vague terms like  noted for
compliance/guidance, therefore, the Committee desires  that the Ministry should furnish Action Taken Notes in  respects of recommendations categorized    in Chapter-IV   in
detail and to the point, as per the intention and spirit of the recommendations of the Committee.
                                   
3.
                  The details of the ATR is being discussed in the succeeding pages.
 
 
CHAPTER – I
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS, WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
INTRODUCTION
 
1.         The Committee notes the trend of growth of SSI sector vis-a-vis Industrial sector.  During 2005-06 the Micro and Small enterprises sector registered a
growth rate of 12.3 per cent as against a growth rate of 8.1 per cent for the overall industrial sector, showing better performance of SSI sector. The Committee
impresses upon the Government to realize the importance of SSI sector which still has large potential to grow. The Committee solicits all out support, from all the
concerned agencies specially the financial institutions to come forward and provide their best services to this sector for its overall growth and recommends the
Ministry to continue its endeavor to bring together all the agencies so as to ensure tapping the growth potential of the SSI sector in the country.
(Para 1.16)
Action taken
2.         The suggestion of the Committee has been noted.  The Ministry shall continue its endeavour for tapping the maximum growth potential of the MSME sector.
 
DEVELOPMENT COMMISSIONER FOR SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES
 

REPORT
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/206threport.htm[04-07-2016 13:17:21]
Recommendation/Observation
 
3.         The Committee also feels that DC’s office needs to be reoriented in view of changing scenario of the day.  The Committee desires that a time frame be set up
for doing so and ensure that DC’s office successfully implements the policies and programmes for promotion and development of SSIs.   It’s role remains incomplete
if it does not provide effective monitoring mechanism.  The Committee accordingly solicits progress report on the functioning of National Board of MSME
constituted under the MSMED Act. 2006.
(Para 3.3)
 
Action taken
4.         The process of reorientation of the Office of the DC (MSME) is in progress. The nomenclature of the Office of the DC (SSI) has been changed to Office of the DC
(MSME).  A new Division, namely National Board for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (NBMSME) has been created in the Office of the DC (MSME) to address the
matters related to NBMSME. A meeting of the Board has already been held on 20 th June 2007 under the Chairmanship of Minister (MSME).  In addition, a “EM Cell” has
been created in MSME Policy division to keep track of the progress made in filing of Memoranda by medium enterprises and also to resolve the problems raised by the
States/UTs in this regard.
 
ROLE OF DC (SSI) IN EXECUTION OF CLUSTER DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
5.         Further the Committee considers the role of DC (SSI) very critical in execution of cluster development programme. The Committee desires that DC’s office
actively involve the beneficiary units through their associations.  The Committee hopes CDPs would certainly result in technology and skill upgradations, increased
production and exports and overall  increase in competitiveness of the clusters. Since the scheme is demand based DC’s office has also to play proactive role in
persuading the States where response is not forthcoming.
(Para 3.4)
 
Action taken
6.         Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises has adopted cluster development approach as a key strategy for enhancing the productivity and competitiveness as
well as capacity building of Micro and Small Enterprises and their collectives in the country, under its scheme of Micro and Small Enterprises Cluster Development
Programme (MSECDP).  Under the cluster development methodology adopted by Office of DC (MSME), existing associations are given due importance and lead role in the
process of implementation of the cluster development programme. The beneficiary units are actively involved in the cluster development process either directly or through
associations.  The diagnostic study report and the action plan for cluster development activities are prepared in consultation with the associations, beneficiary units and other
stakeholders. The action plan is also formally validated by the associations and other stakeholders. Technology and skill upgradation, exports enhancement, quality
upgradation, conservation of resources etc. (through exposure visits, training programmes , seminars, delegation to domestic and international trade exhibitions, technology
transfers, buyer seller meets, etc.) are the regular features of the cluster development approach.   Depending on the needs of the cluster, sufficient activities on technology &
skill upgradation, export promotion, good manufacturing practices, strengthening of associations, support through business development providers are included in the action
plan to achieve the desired targets of cost competitiveness and productivity enhancement.
 
7.         The detailed guidelines of the cluster development scheme were circulated to all the State Governments followed by D.O. letters from AS&DC (MSME) to Secretary
(Inds.) of   State Governments requesting   them to send cluster development proposals in
their respective States. Guidelines have also been uploaded on official website of the Department. States from where no/less proposals have been received are continuously
persuaded through suitable correspondence and meetings to send proposals. Meetings with Associations are also held to motivate them to pose suitable cluster development
proposals.
 
SURPLUS MANPOWER AT LOWER LEVELS
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
8.         The Committee notes that NSIC suffers from surplus manpower at lower levels, which possesses inadequate skills to operate the schemes of the Corporation
that not only lead to high overheads but also does not allow to employ /induct professional staff in required areas like marketing, technology and other vital business
development areas.  The Committee feels that Corporation has to shed its manpower particularly in the lower levels so as to make it a commercial organisation
capable enough to withstand the competitive atmosphere. 
(
Para 4.8)

Action taken
9.         The recommendation of the committee has been noted.  It is pertinent to mention that the Corporation had introduced Voluntary Retirement Scheme.  During last 6
years, 296 employees have availed Voluntary Retirement Scheme, out of which 177 employees were from ‘C’ & ‘D’ categories.
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
10.       The Committee observes that though NSIC is expected to play a pivotal role in area of marketing, the bulk buyers from the Government
Departments/Agencies are not responsive in matters of making purchases through the small scale units registered under NSIC Single Point Registration Scheme.
(Para 4.10)
11.       The Committee therefore, recommends that the Government Departments/ Agencies should declare NSIC a nodal agency for purchases. This will enable
NSIC to play an effective role in marketing the products of the micro and small enterprises.  The Committee also desires the Ministry of SSI to pursue with all the
Government Departments and agencies to declare NSIC nodal agency for purchases.  It will not only make NSIC to play effective role in marketing the products of
micro and small industries but also may generate additional demands for products of SSI units.
(Para 4.11)
 
 
 
 
 
 
Action taken/Comments
12.       NSIC forms consortia of small enterprises manufacturing the identical products and participates in tenders on their behalf, floated by various government departments,
public sector enterprises to secure bulk orders for micro & small enterprises.  These orders are then distributed to these units depending upon their capacity.   As tender
participation by NSIC is to support the marketing efforts of the micro & small enterprises, the bulk buyers (Government Departments and Central Public Sector Undertakings)
should give purchase preference in finalizing those tenders where NSIC’s/MSEs  quote competitive rates or are able to match their prices with other suppliers. This would
enable MSEs to overcome the problem of marketing their products.
 
13.       All Government Departments/Public Sector Undertakings are being requested to adhere to the provisions of the Government Stores Purchase Programme, where
Government of India has been extending various facilities to the MSEs registered with NSIC under its Single Point Registration Scheme.  These facilities inter-alia include the
following:
·
        Issue of tender sets free of cost.
·        Exemption from payment of earnest money
·        Waiver of security deposit up to the monetary limit for which the limit is registered.
·        Price preference up to 15% over the quotation of large scale units.
 
THE MONITORING MECHANISM GOVERNING THE SCHEME
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
14.       The Committee feels that problems like lack of awareness of beneficiary   units, bank managers and reluctance on the part of bankers  need to be addressed
urgently by:
(i)         Organizing awareness programmes/sensitization programmes at various locations all over the country to increase the awareness level of industry
associations, banks and other concerned agencies.
(ii)        Regular review of progress of the scheme in the meetings of State Level   Bankers’ Committees (SLBCs).
(iii)
             Other publicity measures to increase general awareness about the           scheme.   
(Para 10.4)
 
 

REPORT
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/206threport.htm[04-07-2016 13:17:21]
Action taken
15.       As already intimated, awareness programmes/sensitisation programmes at various locations all over the country to increase the awareness level of Industry
Associations, Banks and other concerned agencies are organised by this Ministry through the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Institutes (formerly known
as Small Industries Service Institutes). In organising these programmes concerned nodal agencies/banks, industry associations, primary lending institutions (banks & financial
institutions), industry departments of State and U.T. Governments and other stakeholders are also associated.   Provided the scheme is extended during the current financial
year in the XIth Plan, such programmes will again be organised at various locations all over the country.
 
16.       Progress of the CLCSS is being regularly reviewed in the meetings of the State Level Bankers’ Committees (SLBCs) and the District Level Bankers’ Committees
(DLBCs) meetings.
           
17.       Sufficient copies of the revised guidelines on the CLCSS were printed and distributed through all the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Institutes
(MSME DI), nodal agencies/banks and through the Office of the DC (MSME) to the industry departments and concerned    agencies of   State/ U.T. Governments, banks and
financial institutions, industry associations and entrepreneurs. Provided the extension of the scheme in the financial year 2007-08 in the XIth Plan, other publicity measures
will be taken to increase general awareness about the scheme amongst various stake holders.
 
CLUSTER DEVELOPMENTS
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
18.       The Committee notes that the budget provision estimated for SICDP at Rs.61.20 crores  seems to be appropriate. Further, On the basis of the above 20 new
clusters including four from NE region will be taken up for development comprising of soft interventions and/or hard interventions including setting up of common
facility centres. In addition, Diagnostic studies for identifying the needs of the clusters will also be taken up.  The Committee hopes that the proposed   interventions
in these clusters will result in increase in turn over, exports, employment, level of technological awareness among entrepreneurs, exposure to new technology and
product diversification etc. and also improvement in productivity of the work force, material and marketing practices. The Committee feels that the benefits arising
out of soft intervention may not be immediate and visible but will have a long-term effect in change of mindset of the members of the cluster and  expects that
interventions under SICDP will help the small enterprises to become competitive in the medium to long term.
(Para 14.8)
 
 
Action taken
19.       The observations made by the Committee have been noted.  The interventions in each cluster under Micro and Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme
(MSECDP) are designed on a holistic pattern to ensure continuous trust-building amongst the units and other stakeholders, competitiveness of the beneficiary units, capacity
building, technology and skill upgradation , quality improvement, energy conservation, better compatibility with IPR, etc.   These activities are undertaken by the Cluster
Development Agent (CDA)/Cluster Development Executive (CDEs) with regular handholding support for the cluster members.  Once the cluster becomes mature after soft
interventions like training, exposure visits, etc., the need for the setting up Common Facility Centre (CFC) is also assessed.  The CFC is set up as per the guidelines of
MSECDP.
           
20.       The benefits of the soft interventions on change of mindset of members of the cluster depend on the existing level of technology, cohesiveness between the
stakeholders, trust level, exclusivity of the product range, professionalism of the association, etc.  However, it is expected that by the time soft interventions are over, cluster
will become mature enough to realize the importance of cluster based interventions including hard interventions (CFC) for becoming competitive in the medium to long term.
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
21.       The Committee is constrained to note that credit to micro and small enterprises is still not smooth and adequate.  The Banks still demand collateral security
despite the RBI guidelines.  The Committee feels that the mindset at the branch level of Banks needs to be changed.  In this scenario this scheme covers loans upto
Rs. 25 lakh only  going by the current business trend this needs to be enhanced as many entrepreneurs in this sector would like to go for higher loans and in that
case they have to furnish collateral or third party guarantee. 
(Para 15.10)
 
Action taken
22.       The proposal to enhance the loan limit from Rs.25 lakh to Rs.50 lakh formed a component of the ‘Package for Promotion of Micro and Small Enterprises’. The
Package was approved by Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on October 16, 2006 and announced in the Parliament on February 27, 2007 by the Minister (MSME).

The Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) has issued the necessary circular to all concerned informing the enhancement of the loan limit
from Rs.25 lakh to Rs.50 lakh and has become effective from 2nd  July 2007.
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
23.       The Committee,  therefore, recommends for the following modifications in the Credit Guarantee Scheme  for strengthening of the scheme:
            (i)         Raising the loan limit from Rs.25 lakh to Rs.50 lakh;
(ii)        Raising the guarantee cover from 75% to 80% for micro enterprises for loans upto Rs.5 lakh; and
(iii)   Raising the guarantee cover from 75% to 80% for micro and small        enterprises   owned and/or operated by women.
(Para 15.11)
 
Action taken
24.       All these suggestions were approved by Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on October 16, 2006 and announced in the Parliament on February 27, 2007 by the
Minister (MSME). CGTMSE has issued the necessary circular vide No.36/2007-08 dated 2 July 2007.
 
MDA PROGRAMME
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
25.       The Committee takes note of the MDA programme and observes that the scheme can be successful only when it is given wide publicity through print and
electronic media, circulars to associations and apex trade bodies and SISIs so as to enable more units to take advantage of the scheme.
(Para 16.8)
 
Action taken
26.       The Office of DC (MSME) has already taken action to make MDA programme successful by way of advertising the scheme through print media, circulars to
Association/Apex Trade Bodies and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Institutes, so that more unit could participate in Trade Fairs.
 
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
27.       The Committee observes that in 11 th Five Year Plan the Government envisages to provide hand-holding support to  2 lakh potential entrepreneurs and in
2007-08 only 15,000 potential entrepreneurs will be participating.  The Committee feels that target is very low for 2007-08 and wonders how the 11 th Five Year Plan
targets would be achieved unless these are equally spread over all the five years.
(Para 18.13)
 
Action taken
28.       This is a new scheme for implementation during XI Plan.  Guidelines for scheme are yet to be approved.  During XI Plan hand-holding support to 1,50,000 potential
entrepreneurs is envisaged.  As it may take off in the later part of this year, a lower target of hand-holding support to potential entrepreneurs has been fixed for the year 2007-
08.
 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
29.       The Committee is further constrained to observe that there is no separate monitoring mechanism exclusively for NER and Sikkim.  Secretary (SSI & ARI)
holds review meetings with the senior officers of Small Industries Development Organisation to review the implementation of various Plan schemes.  The Committee
desires  the Ministry to have a separate monitoring mechanism for NE region for overseeing  the  implementation of schemes for promotion of micro and small
enterprises.
(Para 20.7)
 

REPORT
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/206threport.htm[04-07-2016 13:17:21]
Action taken
30.       A separate NER cell has been created in O/o DC (MSME) for monitoring the implementation of schemes in NER and Sikkim.
 
 
CHAPTER – II
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLIES
 
 
RESULT ORIENTED ACTION PLAN
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
1.         The Committee feels these initiatives need to be translated into result oriented actions.  The Committee hopes that action plan prepared by the Ministry of
SSI will certainly take care of the fact.  The Committee would however, like to see the progress in the ATR to be submitted by the Ministry of SSI.
(Para 1.21)
 
Action taken
2.         The initiatives of the Ministry of SSI are generally result oriented. The intermediate outputs and the final outcome of the Schemes are given in the Outcome Budget
2007-08 of the Ministry, which has been laid on the Table of both the Houses.
 
CREDIT RATING SCHEME
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
3.         The Committee notes with concern that allocation for NE  region towards, the grant meant for credit rating scheme has been reduced to Rs. 0.50 crore  as
against Rs. 2.00 crore  in 2006-07.  The Committee feels it may discourage implementation of this scheme.  The Committee desires that Government should accord
due importance to it as has been done in rest of the country.
(Para 4.7)
 
Action taken
4.         For the financial year 2006-07, Government’s budgetary support amounting to Rs.44.95 crore was available to NSIC for various programme /schemes including
operating expenses of its Technical Services Centres.  Under the major head ‘Other Grants’, Rs.2.00 crore was earmarked for the ‘Development of North-Eastern Region’.
There was no specific grant meant for Performance & Credit Rating Scheme under North Eastern Region.
 
5.         During the year 2007-08, budgetary support amounting to Rs.20.00 crore is available to NSIC for two schemes, i.e., Performance & Credit Rating Scheme and
Marketing Assistance Scheme, which are being implemented by NSIC on behalf of the Government. 10% of the outlay (i.e., Rs.2.00 crore – Rs.0.50 under Performance &
Credit Rating Scheme and Rs.1.50 crore under Marketing Assistance Scheme) has been allocated for the Development of N.E. Region.
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
6.         The Committee feels that NSIC has to enlarge its resource base with a view to serve small scale sector and compete with other institutions and Banks engaged
in financing the small sector.  The Committee desires that Ministry and NSIC may find out the ways to enable the Corporation to compete with other financial
institutions.
(Para 4.9)
 
Action taken
7.         The banks & other financial institutions are having strong financial base and expertise for lending to the industrial/service enterprises. NSIC does not have financial
base to compete with the banks and other financial institutions.   Therefore, NSIC has adopted the role of a facilitator and made arrangements with commercial banks to
facilitate the credit needs (long-term as well as working capital requirements) of the micro & small enterprises.  Under these arrangements, NSIC mobilizes the credit

REPORT

proposals of the micro & small enterprises and forwards the same to the banks, with whom, tie-up arrangements have been made, for the purpose of sanctioning the loans to
the applicant units as per their lending norms.
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
8.         The Committee observes that there is a need for strengthening monitoring mechanism of the scheme.  The Committee therefore suggests that :-
 
(i)         RBI may include “review of Credit Guarantee Scheme” as one of the items in its agenda for regular meetings held with commercial banks.
(ii)        Ministry of Finance may create a monitoring mechanism for reviewing the progress made under Credit Guarantee Scheme by Banks.
(iii)       Directorate of Industries in various States may be requested to carry out review of coverage of credit under Credit Guarantee Scheme by banks in
their respective States.
iv)
                Commercial banks may be requested to apprise the Ministry of SSI, regularly, on the progress made by their respective banks under the Credit
Guarantee Scheme.
(Para 15.12)
 
Action taken
9.         The Reserve Bank of India has been apprised of the suggestions of the Committee. Further, the Directorate of Industries in all States/ UTs have been requested review
the progress made under Credit Guarantee Scheme, in association with the banks. The bank-wise progress made under the scheme is being furnished by the CGTMSE to the
Ministry and is reviewed by Secretary (MSME) on monthly basis.
 
 
OTHER SCHEMES
 
Recommendation/Observation
           
10.       The Committee observes that the actual requirement of funds/anticipated expenditure under the scheme of Surveys, Studies and Policy Research was less
than the budgetary allocation whereas the actual requirement of funds / anticipated expenditure under NEDB Scheme and Training Institutions Scheme was more
than the budgetary allocation.  This gives an impression that there was a mismatch between the allocation of funds and actual requirement and therefore not based
on sound budgetary principles.  The Committee advises the Ministry to take precaution while making allocation vis-a –vis requirements to avoid such a situation 
(Para 18.7)
 
Action taken
11.       In BE 2006-07 a plan provision of Rs.200 lakh was made for implementation of the scheme of Surveys, Studies and Policy Research.  14 new subjects of studies at an
estimated cost of Rs.185 lakh were approved by the Committee for 2006-07.  However, due to delay in finalizing/approval of Terms of References only 4 studies at a total
cost of Rs.55,90,974/- were awarded. The actual expenditure during 2006-07 under this scheme was Rs.18,14617/- because only first installment in 3 cases was released
during 2006-07.  This resulted in lower utilization of funds under the scheme of Surveys, Studies and Policy Research during 2006-07.  In BE 2007-08, a plan provision of
Rs.50 lakh has been made.
 
12.       Demands of funds under the scheme NEDB and Training Institution was high during 2006-07. The expenditure under NEDB Scheme was, however, restricted to its
budget provision of Rs.100 lakh and expenditure under the scheme of Training institutions was Rs.510 lakh as against the estimates of Rs.415 lakh. The excess expenditure
included release of Rs.95 lakh to IIE, Guwahati (NE Region). Funds to IIE were released by way of re-appropriation from the NE budget head to ‘Training Institution’.
 
MINI TOOL ROOMS
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
13.       The Tool Rooms are being set up by Government of India and State Governments with an objective to provide the technological support services to SMEs in
the North Eastern Region by providing precision quality toolings and trained manpower in the area of tool engineering.   The Committee feels there is need to
increase tool rooms in the region.  The States have to be persuaded by the Ministry of SSI in this regard.
(Para 21.4)
 
Action taken

REPORT
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/206threport.htm[04-07-2016 13:17:21]
14.       The Government has set up a Tool Room & Training Centre, at Guwahati. In addition, the State Government of Nagaland have recently set up a Tool Room at
Dimapur with financial assistance from GoI, under Mini Tool Room Scheme (a Centrally Sponsored Scheme).
 
15.       The Government also approved a proposal to render financial assistance to State Government of Tripura, for setting up a Mini Tool Room. The State Government has
since withdrawn this proposal.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
CHAPTER – III
 
THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE HAS NOT ACCEPTED REPLIES OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
1.         Considering that the policy package announced for stepping up of credit to SME sector by providing 20% year on year growth in credit flow is a positive
step, still much remains to be done.  The Committee is constrained to observe that number of SSI accounts, have drastically gone down from 29.64 lakh in 1998 to
16.33 lakh in 2003.  However, a slight rise to 18.85 lakh in 2006 is no solace.  Similarly the credit in terms of percentage of Net Banking Credit (NBC) to SSI has also
witnessed the same fate.  It went down from 17.5 % of NBC to 8.1% in 2006.   The Committee is of the considered opinion that the credit to SSI in terms of
percentage of NBC should also not be less than 20% and therefore calls upon the Ministry of SSI and Ministry of Finance, RBI and the Banks to be more

considerate to SSIs for their growth and prosperity in the national interest.
(Para 1.17)
 
Action taken
2.         Though the percentage of credit to MSE sector to net bank credit (NBC) of public and private sector banks has decreased from 10.8% and 9.7% respectively as at the
end of March 2003 to 7.9% and 3.8% respectively as at the end of March 2007, credit to MSE sector by public and private sector banks has increased in absolute terms from
Rs.52,646 crore and Rs.8,051 crore respectively as at the end of March 2003 to Rs.1,04,900 crore and Rs.12,881 crore respectively as at the end of March 2007. So far, the
reported credit data pertained primarily to the manufacturing MSE sector. However, with the enactment of the MSMED Act, 2006, data on credit to services sector will also
need to be incorporated. Since the growth in the services sector has shown a higher rate compared to the manufacturing sector, data on credit to SME sector will reflect a more
realistic position with respect to share in the NBC.
 
3.         Some of the reasons for declining number of accounts of MSE, as informed by the Reserve Bank of India, are as under:-
 
(a)
    Compromise settlement and prudential write off.
(b)   Migration from MSE to medium enterprises.
4.         Besides the bank finance route, some of the new units are adopting new routes of finance such as corporate linked chain financing, venture capital and private equity,
etc.
 
5.         In order to address this issue, all banks (including Regional Rural Banks) have been advised to make concerted efforts to provide credit cover on an average to at least
5 new small/medium enterprises at each of their semi urban/urban branches per year.
 
Further Recommendation
 
6.         The Committee understands that the credit to SME Sector by public and private sector banks has increased in absolute term from Rs.52,646 crore   and
Rs.8,051 crore respectively as at the end of March, 2003 to Rs.1,04,900 crore  and Rs.12,881 crore respectively as at the end of March, 2007 but the Committee is
interested in knowing the progress made in regard to the Government’s declarations of the policy package for stepping up of credit to SME sector by providing
20% year on year growth. The Committee desires that Government should strive in achieving the milestone as set by its own policy.  There is no substance in the
argument of the Ministry of MSME  that the credit size to MSME  has increased, that is but natural, keeping in view the increase in the overall credit volume of the
banks. What matters for critical assessment of credit to SSI sector is the percentage term as the objective has been set by the Policy Package to SME Sector.
 
DEMAND NO. 86
 
ADEQUATE FUNDS TO CREDIT GUARANTEE FUND SCHEME AND MSME CLUSTER DEVELOPMENT SCHEME
 
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
7.         The Committee considers these two schemes i.e. Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme and MSME Cluster Development Scheme as instrumental in promotion and
development of MSMEs.  The Committee does not want these schemes to suffer from budgetary constraints and accordingly impresses upon the Ministry to
aggressively pursue with Planning Commission and Ministry of Finance for adequate funds at RE stage and inform the Committee of the outcome thereof.
(Para 2.2)
 
Action taken
8.         Planning Commission and Ministry of Finance will be requested to provide adequate funds for Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme and MSME Cluster Development
Programme at RE stage. The Committee will be kept informed of the outcome.
 
Further Recommendation
 
9.         Since no time frame has been fixed by the Ministry and the assurance too was given for RE stage of the financial year 2007-08 the Committee will appreciate
if the outcome is reflected in the BE of 2008-09.

MARKET ASSISTANCE SCHEME
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
13.       Market Assistance Scheme is meant for promotion and development of markets for the products of micro and small enterprises.  It is proposed that the NSIC
will organize 5 exhibitions, participate in 45 exhibitions, organize 15 buyer-seller meetings, conduct 150 marketing promotion seminars, conduct 150 intensive
campaigns and conduct 570 market entrepreneurship skill development programmes attracting 2500 candidates. The Ministry proposes to enhance competitiveness
of micro and small enterprises by facilitating them to participate in exhibitions to market their products.  According to the Outcome budget of the Ministry of SSI,
participation in these events would provide micro and small enterprises an exposure to national and international markets. The Committee is of the view that
organizing buyer-seller meetings will enhance venture development skills and improve marketing of products and market promotion seminars will create awareness
of various plans and schemes. The Committee desires that intensive campaigns are required to be organised in both rural and urban areas to have maximum reach. 
(Para 4.6)
Action taken
14.       The recommendation of the Committee has been noted for necessary compliance.
 
 
Further Recommendation
 
15.       The Committee finds that the Action Taken Notes as furnished by Ministry of MSME merely enumerate for necessary compliance for future but the ATN
does not mention anything about the steps taken by the NSIC with regard to organizing exhibitions, meetings, seminars etc. in both rural & urban areas. The
Committee desired that the Ministry may categorically comment on the Committee’s suggestions.
 
Recommendation/Observation
 
16.       NSIC being an all India organisation should be allocated steel, coal and other raw materials for distribution to small enterprises in all States. At present,
allocation of steel is made to NSIC only in those states where SIDCs  do not exist.  Since SSI units are not in a position to approach large producers for smaller
quantities, the Committee feels that NSIC can help overcome this gap if it is facilitated as one of the organisations for distribution of raw materials in all States to
SSIs from organisation like SAIL, RINL, Hindustan Zinc Ltd, Indian Oil Corporation Ltd., Gas Authority of India Ltd., Coal India Ltd. etc. These producers may
accord quantity preference for deliveries to micro & small enterprises sector through NSIC.   The Committee desires that the Ministry take up the matter with the
concerned agencies/bodies with a view to facilitate the SSI units as well as NSIC.
(Para 4.12)

PROVISION FOR THE PROJECTS/SCHEMES FOR THE BENEFIT OF THE NORTH EASTERN REGION AND SIKKIM
 
Recommendation/Observation
           
32.       The Committee is of the view that the North Eastern Region including Sikkim have abundant natural resources and potential for small and tiny units. These
resources needs to be utilized for industrial development. The absence of motivated entrepreneurs has hampered the promotion and rapid industrialization. The
growth of small scale industries in the region has not kept pace with the growth of SSIs in other parts of the country. 
(Para 20.4)
 
Action taken
33.       State Governments of NER and Sikkim are being persuaded to submit viable proposals for the respective plan schemes.  A separate NER cell has been created in O/o
DC (MSME) for monitoring the implementation of schemes in NER and Sikkim.
 
Further Recommendation
 
34.       The Committee is of the considered  view that the abundant natural resources of North-Eastern Region should be appropriately harnessed in the better
interest of the region for comprehensive industrial development. Balanced industrial development is not only essential for economic development of the region but
also for overall industrial progress and development. Only, institutional arrangement for the purpose, as has been done by Ministry of MSME by launching NER
Cell in Office of DC (MSME), won’t be sufficient, rather it would require chalking out `further Action-Plan’ and rigorous implementation thereof.

NATIONAL COMMISSION ON ENTERPRISES IN THE UNORGANIZED/INFORMAL SECTOR      (NCEUS):
 
13.       The Committee feels that the NCEUS has to be proactive in reaching out to the State Governments to make them submit their preliminary proposal
identifying the location for growth pole in more and more States.  The Committee suggest, this must be done in time frame manner.
(Para 19.5)
 
Action taken
14.       The NCEUS has proposed the formation of Growth Poles in pursuance to the Finance Minister’s Budget Speech 2005-06 in different parts of the country with a view
to integrating within a geographical location a number of clusters engaged in manufacturing and/or services that would facilitate expansion of production and employment in
MSEs.
 
15.       In accordance with above, NCEUS requested all State Governments/ UTs to identify multi-product industrial/artisanal/handloom/handicraft clusters that have the
potential to evolve into Growth Poles. The State Governments identified and submitted preliminary proposals to the NCEUS. On the basis of the preliminary proposals from
the State Governments, six pilot  Growth Poles Project, namely, Sikandara in Dausa District (Rajasthan), Chamoli in Uttarakhand, Kollam in Kerala, Panchal and Domjur in
Howrah District (West Bengal), Champa, Jangir in Chhattisgarh and South West Kamprup District in Assam have been initiated by the Commission.
As soon as ‘in principle approval’ is received from the Planning Commision, proposals from other States Governments/ UTs would be called for to identify locations for
Growth Poles.
 
Recommendation/Observation
           
16.       The Committee endorses the following steps taken by Government in order to accelerate the setting up of SSI units in this region :
(i)         Small Industries Services Institutes/Branch Institutes(SISIs/BIs) have been opened in all the North Eastern States & Sikkim.
(ii)        Under the IID Scheme, Central Grant (maximum Rs. 4 crore) is provided to the Implementing Agency for setting up IID Centre in the North Eastern
States and Sikkim as against Rs.2 crore to most of the States in India. 
(iii)       Under the Integrated Infrastructural Development Scheme, thirteen IID Centres have been sanctioned in NE Region. 
(iv)       A Tool Room and Training Centre at Guwahati has been set up to design and manufacture tools, dyes, zigs and fixtures etc. and to impart training in
tool and dye manufacturing, use of computers in design and manufacturing. 
(iv)
             Indian Institute of Entrepreneurship has been set up at Guwahati.
(Para 20.5)
Action taken
